title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing the previous page): a field homomorphism K → K' gives a morphism of étale topoi B_{K'} → B_K and of fundamental groupoids Π_{K'} → Π_K. After choosing compatible separable closures K̄ ⊂ K̄' (K̄ being the separable closure of K inside K̄'), this becomes the restriction map of absolute Galois groups (3) E_{K̄'/K'} → E_{K̄/K}, σ ↦ σ|_{K̄}.

This page determines the image and the kernel of (3).

(i) Image. Let K_1 = K̄ ∩ K' be the separable algebraic closure of K in K'. Grothendieck first wrote "clôture sép.", crossed it out and wrote "alg". Since K_1 ⊂ K̄, the relative closure that matters here is the separable one. By standard Galois theory (natural irrationalities), the image of (3) is the closed subgroup Gal(K̄/K_1).
- If K' is finitely generated over K, then K_1 is a finite extension of K, so the image has finite index [K_1:K].
- The image is all of Gal(K̄/K) iff K_1 = K, i.e. iff K is separably algebraically closed in K'.

(ii) Kernel. The kernel is Gal(K̄'/K̄K'). Under the inserted hypothesis that K' is finitely generated, (3) is injective iff K' is algebraic over K.
- If K' is algebraic over K, then K̄K' is purely inseparable over K̄, hence separably closed, so the kernel is trivial.
- If tr.deg ≥ 1, then K̄K' is a finitely generated function field over a separably closed field. It is not separably closed, so the kernel is nontrivial.

(iii) Bijectivity. Combining (i) and (ii), (3) is bijective iff K' is purely inseparable (radicielle) over K. In characteristic 0 this means K → K' is an isomorphism.

(iv) Conclusion. In characteristic 0, the (2-)functor K ↦ B_K, Π_K, or (K, K̄) ↦ E_{K̄/K} is conservative when restricted to finitely generated extensions K → K'.

Purpose: this is the opening of the anabelian programme for fields in La Longue Marche. The next page specializes to fields finitely generated over Q, asking whether a field is determined by B_K / Π_K and hinting at full faithfulness. It then observes that for arbitrary fields (e.g. separably closed ones) the functor is far from faithful, which motivates a 'finer object' than B_K.
errors: The correction from 'clôture sép.' to 'clôture alg.' is slightly misleading. The relevant field is K_1 = K̄ ∩ K', the separable algebraic closure of K in K'. This matches Grothendieck's own later phrase 'K séparablement alg. clos dans K''. With the algebraic (non-separable) closure, the index statement would be off by inseparable degree.

The added hypothesis 'si K' est ext. de type fini' is genuinely necessary for the injectivity criterion. Counterexample without it: K' = separable closure of K(t) gives a trivial kernel but K' is transcendental. Grothendieck caught this himself with the insertion, so it is not an error in the final text.
No substantive errors otherwise; all claims are standard Galois theory.

ideas.what: Image of Gal(K'^sep/K') → Gal(K^sep/K) equals Gal(K^sep/K_1), with K_1 the relative separable closure of K in K'. It has finite index for finitely generated K'.
ideas.modern_name: Natural irrationalities / restriction of Galois groups
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (functoriality of π_1 of Spec of fields; Exp. V, IX) in essence

ideas.what: Restriction map is injective iff K'/K is algebraic (K' finitely generated), and bijective iff K'/K is purely inseparable.
ideas.modern_name: Galois groups are insensitive to radicial extensions (topological invariance of the étale site)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; SGA1 / SGA4 topological invariance of the étale site

ideas.what: In char 0, K ↦ G_K (or B_K, Π_K) is conservative on finitely generated extensions. This is the first step toward the anabelian question of whether finitely generated fields over Q are determined by their Galois groups.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983, Esquisse 1984); full theorem by Pop (1994), number field case Neukirch–Uchida
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (§ on anabelian geometry), Letter to Faltings (1983); La Longue Marche (unpublished manuscript)

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary Galois-theoretic preliminaries (image, kernel, radicial extensions, conservativity) leading into the well-known birational anabelian question. The obstruction from purely inseparable extensions in char p is also well known (the Frobenius-twist issue in Pop/Stix). Nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 1–2: likely 'K_1 de K̄/K, clôture alg. [over crossed 'sép.'] de K dans K'' — mathematically it is the separable closure K_1 = K̄ ∩ K'.
Last lines: probably 'conservatif quand on se limite aux homomorphismes de corps K → K' (de car. 0) pour lesquels K' est une ext. de type fini de K'; 'à ceux pour' seems to be a reworded fragment.
